title: Review: feat: add crypto2dev CryptoCb port for TLS integration
description: Pre-merge code review of the crypto2dev CryptoCb shim (two commits: feat port + AWS CI script). Covers correctness, maintainer risk, efficiency, elegance, and decisions worth defending.
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — The double-close pool bug is under a documented invariant so won't fire in practice; the biggest day-to-day risks are the AesGcmSetKey footgun and the g_tls_safe_mode global behavior, both of which will generate repeated user confusion. The CI script is purely a personal tool issue.
Confidence: 25% chance of missed bug. Uncertainty driven by: (1) AES-CTR endianness — the counter increment code looks correct for big-endian CTR (the RFC standard) but I cannot verify the hardware driver's counter behavior without reading the kernel module source; (2) wc_CryptoCb_RegisterDevice idempotency — the double-registration in assign_devid* paths is probably fine but depends on wolfSSL internals I haven't read; (3) no test exercises multi-call AES-CTR or multi-call AES-CBC chaining across multiple wc_AesCbcEncrypt calls. Would raise confidence if: kernel module source reviewed to confirm CTR counter endianness, multi-call AES-CTR KAT added with independently computed expected values.
